title: Math Material — Cone Cross-Section: Radius and Area
question: How do the radius and area of a horizontal cut through a 30° cone depend on the distance from the apex, and for which distances is the area defined?
intro:
A cone has a circular base with a fixed radius \(R\). The angle between the cone's vertical axis and its sloping side is \(30^\circ\).

A horizontal cut at distance \(h\) below the apex makes a smaller circle with radius \(x\).
figure_alt: Cone with a 30° angle between the axis and the sloping side; a horizontal cut at distance h below the apex has radius x; the base has radius R

questions.title: Radius of the smaller circle
questions.prompt: Express the radius \(x\) of the smaller circle as a function of \(h\).
steps:
The axis, the radius \(x\) and the sloping side form a right triangle with a \(30^\circ\) angle at the apex:

\[
\tan30^\circ=\frac{x}{h}
\]

questions.title: Area of the smaller circle
questions.prompt: Write the area of the smaller circle, \(A_c(h)\), as a function of \(h\).
steps:
The smaller circle has radius \(x(h)\):

\[
A_c=\pi x^2
\]

questions.title: Domain in terms of R
questions.prompt: Determine the domain of \(A_c(h)\) in terms of the fixed base radius \(R\).
steps:
The smaller circle grows from a point at the apex to the base circle:

\[
0\le A_c(h)\le\pi R^2
\]

Since \(h\ge0\):

\[
\boxed{0\le h\le\sqrt3\,R}
\]

Check: at \(h=\sqrt3\,R\), \(x=\dfrac{\sqrt3\,R}{\sqrt3}=R\), the base circle.
